title: The Wobbly Caterpillar's Surprise
markdown:
Sunbeams danced, and the forest smelled sweet as berries. Noah the jewel-feathered bird was tidying his nest when he spotted Buttons, a fluffy bear cub. Ranger Tess, eyes sparkling, watched them both.

“Look!” Noah pointed to a tiny green caterpillar munching a leaf.

“It’s wiggly!” rumbled Buttons.

The caterpillar munched and munched, a little bigger each day. Noah nudged juicy leaves closer. Buttons sat nearby and tried not to sit on the leaf.

Then one morning the caterpillar was gone. “Where did it go?”

“Don’t worry,” said Tess. “It’s changing. Look on that twig.”

Hanging there: a silky house. The caterpillar had spun it to sleep and change inside. They watched with wonder. Noah counted days on his claws. Buttons counted by tummy-rumbles, which was less accurate.

After many days, a wiggle. A tiny crack. Out came a butterfly, wings bright blue and sunny yellow.

“Wow!” gasped Noah.

“Beautiful!” rumbled Buttons.

WHOOSH. The butterfly flew up, up, up.

“It wasn’t just a crawler!” chirped Noah.

“And it didn’t float like a puff!” giggled Buttons.

Tess smiled. “It didn’t disappear. A big change. First it crawled, then it rested, now it flies.” She named it once: a life cycle. Eating, sleeping, flying. She did not call it changing clothes or the most beautiful thing of all.

Buttons hugged his tummy. “It changed its whole self. Like magic, but real.”

Noah imagined the picture: munch, silk, wings. They left the empty silk house on the twig, so the next curious pair would have a clue. The butterfly was already a speck. Tess packed no sermon. Buttons saved one juicy leaf, just in case another wiggly visitor arrived.
